text: (-)-Epicatechin, a dietary flavan-3-ol and prodrug of apocynin-like NADPH oxidase inhibitors, is oxidized by human myeloperoxidase (MPO). Stopped-flow kinetics show it is among the most efficient electron donors for heme peroxidases, with second-order rate constants for MPO compound I→II and compound II→resting enzyme of 1.9×10⁷ and 4.5×10⁶ M⁻¹s⁻¹ (pH 7, 25 °C), indicating fast one-electron oxidation. Separately, Sestrin2 suppresses uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1) expression: transgenic adipose Sestrin2 overexpression inhibited basal and cold-induced Ucp1 in interscapular brown adipose tissue, reducing thermogenesis and increasing fat accumulation, while Sestrin2⁻/⁻ BAT showed elevated Ucp1. A redox-inactive Sestrin2 mutant was ineffective. Antioxidants (butylated hydroxyanisole, N-acetylcysteine) likewise inhibited cold/cAMP-induced Ucp1. Sestrin2 and antioxidants act by suppressing ROS-mediated p38 MAPK activation.
